nodes.title: Kollaps: Decentralized and Dynamic Topology Emulation
nodes.cite: P. Gouveia, J. Neves, C. Segarra, L. Liechti, S. Issa, V. Schiavoni, M. Matos, 2020. Proc. ACM EuroSys 2020. DOI 10.1145/3342195.3387540.
nodes.note: Decentralized container-based emulator that reproduces end-to-end path properties from a high-level Thunderstorm specification (using tc/eBPF) without a central bottleneck, enabling large dynamic distributed-systems experiments. Contrasts with centralized Mininet/MaxiNet.

nodes.title: TimeKeeper: A Lightweight Virtual Time System for Linux
nodes.cite: J. Lamps, D. M. Nicol, M. Caesar, 2014. Proc. ACM SIGSIM-PADS 2014, pp. 179-186. DOI 10.1145/2601381.2601395.
nodes.note: Kernel-level virtual-time (time-dilation) system that embeds Linux containers in a controllable clock so emulation of high-speed links stays temporally faithful; integrates with Mininet, CORE, EMANE, and ns-3. Foundational virtual-time-correction work for the cluster.

nodes.title: GARNET: A Detailed On-Chip Network Model Inside a Full-System Simulator
nodes.cite: N. Agarwal, T. Krishna, L.-S. Peh, N.K. Jha, 2009. Proc. IEEE ISPASS, pp. 33-42. DOI 10.1109/ISPASS.2009.4919636.
nodes.note: Seminal cycle-accurate on-chip-network model embedded in a full-system simulator (originally GEMS, now gem5's Ruby); its successor Garnet2.0 is gem5's default NoC model. Foundational for coupling interconnect microarchitecture with full-system memory/coherence traffic, and paired with BookSim for NoC research.

nodes.title: ASTRA-SIM: Enabling SW/HW Co-Design Exploration for Distributed DL Training Platforms
nodes.cite: S. Rashidi, S. Sridharan, S. Srinivasan, T. Krishna, 2020. Proc. IEEE ISPASS, pp. 81-92. DOI 10.1109/ISPASS48437.2020.00018.
nodes.note: Simulator of distributed deep-learning training platforms, modeling collective communication over scale-up/scale-out fabrics for algorithm-topology co-design; extended by ASTRA-sim2.0 (Won et al., ISPASS 2023). A systems-boundary tool for the network-of-accelerators era, complementary to gem5/SST node models.

nodes.title: DRAMSim2: A Cycle Accurate Memory System Simulator
nodes.cite: P. Rosenfeld, E. Cooper-Balis, B. Jacob, 2011. IEEE Computer Architecture Letters 10(1):16-19. DOI 10.1109/L-CA.2011.4.
nodes.note: Widely-used cycle-accurate DDR2/3 memory-system model validated against manufacturer Verilog, usable in full-system or trace mode; the standard memory back-end integrated into gem5, SST, and MARSSx86, later superseded for extensibility by Ramulator.

nodes.title: Ramulator: A Fast and Extensible DRAM Simulator
nodes.cite: Y. Kim, W. Yang, O. Mutlu, 2016. IEEE Computer Architecture Letters 15(1):45-49. DOI 10.1109/LCA.2015.2414456.
nodes.note: Fast, template-based DRAM simulator with out-of-the-box support for many standards (DDR3/4, LPDDR, GDDR5, HBM, WIO); ~2.5x faster than prior tools and the modern successor to DRAMSim2. Rebuilt as Ramulator 2.0 (Luo et al., IEEE CAL 2023, DOI 10.1109/LCA.2023.3333759).

nodes.title: The DiskSim Simulation Environment Version 4.0 Reference Manual
nodes.cite: J.S. Bucy, J. Schindler, S.W. Schlosser, G.R. Ganger, 2008. Technical Report CMU-PDL-08-101, Carnegie Mellon Univ. Parallel Data Lab.
nodes.note: The canonical, heavily-validated storage-subsystem simulator (disks, controllers, buses, request schedulers, block caches, RAID); the reference disk/storage-I/O model for decades of file-system and storage research. Systems-boundary counterpart to the memory (DRAMSim/Ramulator) and interconnect (BookSim/Garnet) simulators.

nodes.title: iFogSim2: An Extended iFogSim Simulator for Mobility, Clustering, and Microservice Management in Edge and Fog Computing Environments
nodes.cite: R. Mahmud, S. Pallewatta, M. Goudarzi, R. Buyya, 2022. Journal of Systems and Software 190:111351. DOI 10.1016/j.jss.2022.111351.
nodes.note: Extends and supersedes iFogSim with device mobility (real EUA mobility traces), dynamic distributed cluster formation, and microservice orchestration/migration; the current state of the CloudSim-lineage fog simulators.

nodes.title: GreenCloud: A Packet-Level Simulator of Energy-Aware Cloud Computing Data Centers
nodes.cite: D. Kliazovich, P. Bouvry, S. U. Khan, 2012. The Journal of Supercomputing 62(3):1263-1283. DOI 10.1007/s11227-010-0504-1. (Earlier: IEEE GLOBECOM 2010.)
nodes.note: Packet-level, energy-aware data-center simulator implemented as an ns-2 extension, capturing server/switch/link power (DVFS/DNS power management) with full communication detail; a networking-detailed contrast to CloudSim's coarse event model for two/three-tier DC topologies.

nodes.title: PeerSim: A Scalable P2P Simulator
nodes.cite: A. Montresor, M. Jelasity, 2009. Proc. IEEE Ninth International Conference on Peer-to-Peer Computing (P2P 2009). (Tool: peersim.sourceforge.net.)
nodes.note: The canonical highly-scalable P2P/overlay simulator (cycle-driven and event-driven engines) for gossip, epidemic and churn/failure protocols; still load-bearing for decentralized cloud/edge, DHT and blockchain-overlay simulation. Tagged parallel-distributed-sim since it is P2P rather than data-center, but included by the cloud-DC cluster for the decentralized-infrastructure dimension.

nodes.title: BigHouse: A Simulation Infrastructure for Data Center Systems
nodes.cite: D. Meisner, J. Wu, T. F. Wenisch, 2012. Proc. IEEE Int. Symp. on Performance Analysis of Systems and Software (ISPASS 2012). DOI 10.1109/ISPASS.2012.6189204.
nodes.note: Best-paper Statistical Queuing Simulation (SQS) infrastructure that models datacenter server systems from empirical arrival/service distributions rather than microarchitecture, enabling power-provisioning and latency studies in minutes; a queuing-theory/stochastic-DES methodology complementing the CloudSim-style simulators here.

nodes.title: Batsim: A Realistic Language-Independent Resources and Jobs Management Systems Simulator
nodes.cite: P.-F. Dutot, M. Mercier, M. Poquet, O. Richard, 2016. Proc. Job Scheduling Strategies for Parallel Processing (JSSPP 2016), LNCS vol. 10353, Springer. DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-61756-5_10.
nodes.note: SimGrid-based, language-independent simulator for HPC/cluster/datacenter resource-and-job management (RJMS); its companion scheduler 'batsched' supplies pluggable scheduling policies over a simple event protocol. Built on SimGrid (Casanova, Giersch, Legrand, Quinson, Suter, JPDC 74(10):2899-2917, 2014, DOI 10.1016/j.jpdc.2014.06.008), the foundational versatile distributed-systems simulation substrate.

nodes.title: Simulating Fog and Edge Computing Scenarios: An Overview and Research Challenges
nodes.cite: S. Svorobej, P. Takako Endo, M. Bendechache, C. Filelis-Papadopoulos, K. M. Giannoutakis, G. A. Gravvanis, D. Tzovaras, J. Byrne, T. Lynn, 2019. Future Internet 11(3):55. DOI 10.3390/fi11030055.
nodes.note: Comparative overview and taxonomy of fog/edge simulation tools (iFogSim, EdgeCloudSim, YAFS, and deployment-planners such as FogTorchPI/Brogi & Forti) with open research challenges; a natural survey-of anchor tying together the edge/fog tools in this cluster.

nodes.title: m3: Accurate Flow-Level Performance Estimation using Machine Learning
nodes.cite: C. Li, A. Nasr-Esfahany, K. Zhao, K. Noorbakhsh, P. Goyal, M. Alizadeh, T. Anderson, 2024. Proc. ACM SIGCOMM 2024. DOI 10.1145/3651890.3672243.
nodes.note: Couples a fast flow-level fluid simulation with an ML model to predict data-center tail latency, running 4-8x faster than Parsimon at ~8% median error. Accelerates/supersedes the Parsimon parallel-simulation baseline and is the predecessor of m4 from the same MIT/UW/MSR group.

nodes.title: m4: A Learned Flow-level Network Simulator
nodes.cite: C. Li, A. A. Zabreyko, O. Chabra, A. Nasr-Esfahany, K. Zhao, P. Goyal, M. Alizadeh, T. Anderson, 2025. arXiv:2503.01770 (preprint).
nodes.note: A fully learned flow-level simulator whose neural architecture decomposes state transitions into spatial and temporal components, reaching up to ~100x speedup over packet-level simulation while cutting flow-error vs traditional fluid models. Successor to m3 and a canonical example of a genuine learned (not surrogate-of-metrics) network simulator.

nodes.title: NetworkGym: Reinforcement Learning Environments for Multi-Access Traffic Management in Network Simulation
nodes.cite: M. Haider, M. Yin, M. Zhang, A. Gupta, J. Zhu, Y.-X. Wang, 2024. NeurIPS 2024 (Datasets & Benchmarks Track). arXiv:2411.04138. (Intel Labs / UC Santa Barbara.)
nodes.note: A Simulation-as-a-Service framework providing high-fidelity full-stack RL environments (e.g. multi-access traffic splitting) with an offline-RL benchmark, published in the NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks track. Modern standardized counterpart to ns3-gym and Park for network-RL evaluation.

nodes.title: Differentiable Discrete Event Simulation for Queuing Network Control
nodes.cite: E. Che, J. Dong, H. Namkoong, 2024. arXiv:2409.03740 (preprint; Columbia University).
nodes.note: Makes discrete-event queueing-network simulation differentiable via a smoothing technique, enabling GPU-parallel pathwise policy gradients with 50-1000x better sample efficiency than RL for congestion/scheduling control. A distinct simulation-methodology thread (differentiable DES) complementing the surrogate-GNN and learned-simulator lines.

nodes.title: Graph Neural Networks for Communication Networks: Context, Use Cases and Opportunities
nodes.cite: J. Suarez-Varela, P. Almasan, M. Ferriol-Galmes, K. Rusek, A. Cabellos-Aparicio, P. Barlet-Ros, et al., 2023. IEEE Network 37(3):146-153. arXiv:2112.14792.
nodes.note: Vision-and-use-case survey of GNNs for network modeling, control and management from the RouteNet (BNN-UPC) group. Frames RouteNet-Erlang/Fermi and IGNNITION within the broader learned-network-model agenda; complements Jiang's taxonomy survey.

nodes.title: Exploring the "Internet from space" with Hypatia
nodes.cite: S. Kassing, D. Bhattacherjee, A. B. Águas, J. E. Saethre, A. Singla, 2020. Proc. ACM Internet Measurement Conference (IMC), pp. 214-229. DOI 10.1145/3419394.3423635.
nodes.note: Packet-level LEO constellation simulator pairing a Python constellation/routing generator (satgenpy) with an ns-3 packet-level engine and visualization; the de facto reference tool for 'Internet-from-space' studies and the baseline that StarryNet and xeoverse benchmark against.

nodes.title: StarPerf: Characterizing Network Performance for Emerging Mega-Constellations
nodes.cite: Z. Lai, H. Li, et al. (Tsinghua Univ.), 2020. Proc. IEEE Intl. Conf. on Network Protocols (ICNP). IEEE Xplore doc. 9259357.
nodes.note: Analytical mega-constellation performance simulator that estimates area-to-area latency/throughput/coverage via constellation abstraction and 'constellation scaling' without exchanging packets; complements packet-level Hypatia with fast what-if topology exploration.

nodes.title: SILLEO-SCNS: Network Simulator for Large Low Earth Orbit Satellite Networks
nodes.cite: B. S. Kempton, A. Riedl, 2021. Proc. IEEE Intl. Conf. on Communications (ICC). IEEE Xplore doc. 9500439.
nodes.note: Standalone Python/VTK simulator for large LEO constellations focused on inter-satellite and satellite-ground link design and shortest-path latency (Dijkstra/Floyd-Warshall over SGP4 orbits); a routing-study companion to Hypatia, and forked for Mars-constellation work.

nodes.title: OS3: The CNI Open Source Satellite Simulator (OMNeT++)
nodes.cite: B. Niehoefer, S. Subik, C. Wietfeld, 2013. Proc. 6th Intl. ICST Conf. on Simulation Tools and Techniques (SIMUTools). DOI 10.4108/icst.simutools.2013.251580.
nodes.note: Foundational OMNeT++/INET open-source satellite simulator with SGP4/SDP4 mobility, real TLE track import, weather and channel modeling; the base later extended to LEO constellations by Valentine & Parisis' leosatellites module.

nodes.title: SNS3: Satellite Network Simulator 3 (ns-3 satellite module)
nodes.cite: J. Puttonen et al. (Magister Solutions, ESA contract), 2014. 'Satellite Model for Network Simulator 3,' Proc. SIMUTools 2014 / WNS3. DOI 10.4108/icst.simutools.2014.254631.
nodes.note: ESA-funded ns-3 module implementing DVB-S2 forward and DVB-RCS2 return links with SINR-BLER PHY abstraction, ACM, DAMA capacity categories and random access; the canonical GEO/broadband-satellite counterpart to the LEO-focused ns-3 tools in this cluster.

nodes.title: StarryNet: Empowering Researchers to Evaluate Futuristic Integrated Space and Terrestrial Networks
nodes.cite: Z. Lai, H. Li, et al. (Tsinghua Univ.), 2023. Proc. USENIX Symp. on Networked Systems Design and Implementation (NSDI).
nodes.note: Docker-container emulation framework that builds a real-data-driven digital twin of integrated space-terrestrial networks (ISTNs), running real network stacks over emulated ISLs/GSLs (SGP4 + Skyfield); a key ISTN experimentation platform benchmarked against Hypatia and xeoverse.

nodes.title: A System Simulator for 5G Non-Terrestrial Network Evaluations
nodes.cite: J. Puttonen, L. Sormunen, H. Martikainen, S. Rantanen, J. Kurjenniemi, 2021. Proc. IEEE WoWMoM (NTN-in-6G workshop). IEEE Xplore doc. 9469494.
nodes.note: System-level simulator (Magister) for 5G NR non-terrestrial networks following 3GPP TR 38.811/38.821 channel and geometry assumptions, evaluating NTN UE and cell throughput; a 3GPP-compliant NTN evaluation framework distinct from the already-covered 5G-LENA.

nodes.title: xeoverse: A Real-time Simulation Platform for Large LEO Satellite Mega-Constellations
nodes.cite: M. M. Kassem, N. Sastry (Univ. of Surrey), 2024. arXiv:2406.11366.
nodes.note: Mininet/VM real-time simulator (1 simulated second = 1 wall-clock second) for large LEO mega-constellations, using precomputed topology/routing and incremental ISL updates; reports ~2.9x and ~40x total-runtime speedups over Hypatia and StarryNet respectively.

nodes.title: Developing and Experimenting with LEO Satellite Constellations in OMNeT++
nodes.cite: A. Valentine, G. Parisis (Univ. of Sussex), 2021. Proc. 8th OMNeT++ Community Summit. arXiv:2109.12046.
nodes.note: OMNeT++/INET LEO constellation model (leosatellites) that extends OS3 ported to INET 4.3, validated against FCC-filed constellations for end-to-end ping latency; the OMNeT++ path to LEO constellation simulation and a direct descendant of OS3.

nodes.title: LEO Satellite Networking Relaunched: Survey and Current Research Challenges
nodes.cite: C. Westphal, L. Han, R. Li, 2023. arXiv:2310.07646; also ITU J. Future and Evolving Technologies 4(4).
nodes.note: Broad survey of LEO satellite networking spanning routing, SDN, ML and green networking, plus the state of 3GPP and IETF standardization for ISL-based LEO networks; contextualizes this cluster's simulators within the wider research agenda.

nodes.title: Efficient optimistic parallel simulations using reverse computation
nodes.cite: C. D. Carothers, K. S. Perumalla, R. M. Fujimoto, 1999. ACM Trans. Modeling and Computer Simulation (TOMACS) 9(3):224-253. DOI 10.1145/347823.347828.
nodes.note: Introduces reverse computation as a memory-frugal alternative to state-saving for Time Warp rollback, the defining method behind ROSS and the extreme-scale Warp Speed result. A foundational synchronization-methodology paper distinct from the Fujimoto PDES survey already in corpus.

nodes.title: The Georgia Tech Network Simulator (GTNetS)
nodes.cite: G. F. Riley, 2003. Proc. ACM SIGCOMM Workshop on Models, Methods and Tools for Reproducible Network Research (MoMeTools). DOI 10.1145/944773.944775.
nodes.note: Object-oriented C++ packet-level network simulator built for very-large-scale, MPI-parallel execution (hundreds of thousands of elements), whose scalability lineage feeds directly into ns-3's distributed design. A canonical MPI-based parallel net-sim tool beyond the ns-3/OMNeT++ basics already covered.

nodes.title: A generic framework for parallelization of network simulations (PDNS)
nodes.cite: G. F. Riley, R. M. Fujimoto, M. H. Ammar, 1999. Proc. MASCOTS'99, pp. 128-135.
nodes.note: Defines the federation approach that became Parallel/Distributed ns (PDNS), parallelizing the sequential ns-2 simulator over MPI and scaling to ~250k network elements. Foundational for conservative-synchronized packet-level network simulation and a companion to GTNetS.

nodes.title: A Simulator for Large-Scale Parallel Computer Architectures (SST/macro)
nodes.cite: C. L. Janssen, H. Adalsteinsson, S. Cranford, J. P. Kenny, A. Pinar, D. A. Evensky, J. Mayo, 2010. Int. J. Distributed Systems and Technologies (IJDST) 1(2):57-73.
nodes.note: The macroscale (SST/macro) element of Sandia's Structural Simulation Toolkit: a coarse-grained PDES that runs skeletonized applications over modeled HPC interconnects for extreme-scale network/architecture co-design. Complements ROSS/CODES on the HPC-interconnect side of network M&S.

nodes.title: An Object-Oriented Time Warp Simulation Kernel (WARPED)
nodes.cite: R. Radhakrishnan, D. E. Martin, M. Chetlur, D. M. Rao, P. A. Wilsey, 1998. Proc. ISCOPE'98, Springer LNCS 1505. DOI 10.1007/3-540-49372-7_2.
nodes.note: Openly available, configurable Time Warp kernel (C++/MPI) providing a testbed for optimistic-synchronization optimizations; its modern redesign warped2 continues the line. Implements Jefferson's Time Warp and is a canonical experimentation platform alongside ROSS.

nodes.title: μsik - A micro-kernel for parallel/distributed simulation systems
nodes.cite: K. S. Perumalla, 2005. Proc. 19th Workshop on Principles of Advanced and Distributed Simulation (PADS'05), pp. 59-68. DOI 10.1109/PADS.2005.1.
nodes.note: Micro-kernel PDES architecture that unifies conservative (lookahead) and optimistic (state-saving) synchronization within one system, letting processes even switch mechanisms dynamically. Directly addresses the conservative-vs-optimistic axis central to this cluster.

nodes.title: Warp Speed: Executing Time Warp on 1,966,080 Cores
nodes.cite: P. D. Barnes Jr., C. D. Carothers, D. R. Jefferson, J. M. LaPre, 2013. Proc. 2013 ACM SIGSIM Conf. on Principles of Advanced Discrete Simulation (SIGSIM-PADS). DOI 10.1145/2486092.2486134.
nodes.note: Landmark strong-scaling study running ROSS Time Warp + reverse computation on ~2M Blue Gene/Q cores (PHOLD at ~504 billion events/s). The reference demonstration that optimistic PDES scales to full-machine supercomputers.

nodes.title: Conservative Synchronization of Large-Scale Network Simulations
nodes.cite: A. Park, R. M. Fujimoto, K. S. Perumalla, 2004. Proc. 18th Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Simulation (PADS'04), pp. 153-161. DOI 10.1145/1013329.1013355.
nodes.note: Analytical and experimental comparison of synchronous vs asynchronous null-message conservative algorithms for parallel packet-level network simulation. The conservative-synchronization counterpart to the optimistic works here, grounded in network M&S.

nodes.title: Stochastic Theory of a Data-Handling System with Multiple Sources
nodes.cite: D. Anick, D. Mitra, M. M. Sondhi, 1982. Bell System Technical Journal 61(8):1871-1894. DOI 10.1002/j.1538-7305.1982.tb03089.x.
nodes.note: The foundational fluid-queue model: a buffer fed by many independent on/off exponential sources, solved via a spectral/ODE decomposition. It is the analytical ancestor of essentially all later fluid models of multiplexed traffic (e.g. Misra-Gong-Towsley) and of effective-bandwidth theory.

nodes.title: A Unified Framework for Simulating Markovian Models of Highly Dependable Systems
nodes.cite: A. Goyal, P. Shahabuddin, P. Heidelberger, V. F. Nicola, P. W. Glynn, 1992. IEEE Transactions on Computers 41(1):36-51. DOI 10.1109/12.123381.
nodes.note: Canonical importance-sampling (failure-biasing) framework for simulating rare failure events in Markovian dependability/reliability models, achieving many-orders-of-magnitude speedups. The reliability-side counterpart to queueing rare-event methods and a keystone cited throughout the Heidelberger and Juneja-Shahabuddin surveys.

nodes.title: RESTART: A Method for Accelerating Rare Event Simulations
nodes.cite: M. Villen-Altamirano, J. Villen-Altamirano, 1991. Proc. 13th International Teletraffic Congress (ITC-13), Copenhagen; North-Holland.
nodes.note: The original importance-splitting method for network rare events (buffer overflow, cell loss): trajectories are split into retrials each time they up-cross a threshold toward the rare set. Foundational for all later multilevel-splitting theory (Glasserman et al., L'Ecuyer et al.) and heavily applied in teletraffic simulation.

nodes.title: Fast Simulation of Rare Events in Queueing and Reliability Models
nodes.cite: P. Heidelberger, 1995. ACM Transactions on Modeling and Computer Simulation (TOMACS) 5(1):43-85. DOI 10.1145/203091.203094.
nodes.note: The classic survey/tutorial of importance-sampling techniques for estimating rare events (buffer overflow, system failure) in queueing and reliability simulation. Anchors the rare-event methodology literature and is broadened/updated by the Juneja-Shahabuddin (2006) survey.

nodes.title: Multilevel Splitting for Estimating Rare Event Probabilities
nodes.cite: P. Glasserman, P. Heidelberger, P. Shahabuddin, T. Zajic, 1999. Operations Research 47(4):585-600. DOI 10.1287/opre.47.4.585.
nodes.note: The keystone theoretical analysis of multilevel splitting, deriving conditions for efficiency and near-optimal splitting factors. It formalizes and generalizes RESTART and underpins later adaptive-splitting methods; a load-bearing 'supersedes/formalizes' target for the splitting thread.

nodes.title: Fluid-based Analysis of a Network of AQM Routers Supporting TCP Flows with an Application to RED
nodes.cite: V. Misra, W.-B. Gong, D. Towsley, 2000. Proc. ACM SIGCOMM; Computer Communication Review 30(4):151-160. DOI 10.1145/347059.347421.
nodes.note: THE fluid model of TCP/AQM networks: jump-process stochastic differential equations reduced to coupled ODEs capturing TCP window dynamics and RED, enabling scalable analysis where packet simulation is intractable. Parent work of hybrid fluid/packet simulators (Gu-Liu-Towsley) and a foundation for AQM control-theoretic analysis.

nodes.title: On Integrating Fluid Models with Packet Simulation
nodes.cite: Y. Gu, Y. Liu, D. Towsley, 2004. Proc. IEEE INFOCOM, pp. 2856-2866. DOI 10.1109/INFCOM.2004.1354702.
nodes.note: Hybrid simulation that couples time-stepped fluid models with event-driven packet simulation, keeping fluid-scale efficiency while retaining packet-level detail for flows of interest. Directly applies the Misra-Gong-Towsley fluid framework inside a discrete-event simulator; a core reference for hybrid fluid/packet methodology.

nodes.title: Rare-Event Simulation Techniques: An Introduction and Recent Advances
nodes.cite: S. Juneja, P. Shahabuddin, 2006. In Handbooks in Operations Research and Management Science, Vol. 13: Simulation (eds. S. G. Henderson, B. L. Nelson), Elsevier, pp. 291-350. DOI 10.1016/S0927-0507(06)13011-X.
nodes.note: The authoritative modern survey of rare-event simulation, covering light- and heavy-tailed importance sampling, splitting, and applications to queues and queueing networks. The go-to reference that broadens and updates Heidelberger (1995); a natural 'survey of' hub for the rare-event cluster.

nodes.title: A Class of Mean Field Interaction Models for Computer and Communication Systems
nodes.cite: M. Benaim, J.-Y. Le Boudec, 2008. Performance Evaluation 65:823-838.
nodes.note: Foundational mean-field framework proving that N interacting objects converge to a deterministic (ODE) mean-field limit, giving a scalable modeling alternative to per-node simulation of large systems (MAC protocols, epidemics, caching). Load-bearing for the mean-field/decoupling line of large-network analysis. DOI omitted (not confidently recalled); volume/pages web-confirmed.

nodes.title: Rare Event Simulation using Monte Carlo Methods
nodes.note: The comprehensive edited reference on rare-event Monte Carlo (importance sampling and splitting) with applications to dependability and telecommunication networks. The book-length anchor for this cluster, gathering the RESTART/multilevel-splitting/cross-entropy threads into one volume.

nodes.title: A Survey on Artifacts from CoNEXT, ICN, IMC, and SIGCOMM Conferences in 2017
nodes.cite: M. Flittner, M. N. Mahfoudi, D. Saucez, M. Waehlisch, L. Iannone, V. Bajpai, A. Afanasyev, 2018. ACM SIGCOMM Computer Communication Review 48(1):75-80. DOI 10.1145/3211852.3211864.
nodes.note: Empirical survey assessing artifact availability and reproducibility across four top ACM networking venues, part of the movement that established ACM artifact review/badging in networking. The reproducibility/artifact-evaluation companion to simulation- and measurement-based network studies.

nodes.title: PRISM 4.0: Verification of Probabilistic Real-Time Systems
nodes.cite: M. Kwiatkowska, G. Norman, D. Parker, 2011. Proc. CAV 2011, LNCS 6806, pp. 585-591, Springer. DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-22110-1_47.
nodes.note: The de facto probabilistic model checker for DTMCs, CTMCs, MDPs and probabilistic timed automata; the standard tool applied to randomised protocols (Bluetooth, Zigbee, CSMA/CD) that most network-protocol PMC studies build on. Reference implementation underpinning the Duflot et al. communication-protocol survey; performance-superseded by Storm.

nodes.title: A Storm is Coming: A Modern Probabilistic Model Checker
nodes.cite: C. Dehnert, S. Junges, J.-P. Katoen, M. Volk, 2017. Proc. CAV 2017, LNCS, pp. 592-600, Springer. DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-63390-9_31. Journal version: Hensel et al., 'The probabilistic model checker Storm', STTT 2022, DOI 10.1007/s10009-021-00633-z.
nodes.note: A modern, high-performance probabilistic model checker supporting PRISM/JANI models, GSPNs and dynamic fault trees with a Python API; positioned as the performance-oriented successor/competitor to PRISM for large Markov-model verification.

nodes.title: A Tutorial on Uppaal (timed-automata model checker)
nodes.cite: G. Behrmann, A. David, K. G. Larsen, 2004. In Formal Methods for the Design of Real-Time Systems (SFM-RT 2004), LNCS 3185, pp. 200-236, Springer. DOI 10.1007/978-3-540-30080-9_7. Tool: uppaal.org.
nodes.note: The canonical model checker for networks of timed automata, the workhorse for verifying real-time protocols and schedulers; foundational to the timed-automata line that PRISM's PTA support and UPPAAL SMC extend. This tutorial is the standard entry reference for the tool.

nodes.title: PRISM-games 3.0: Stochastic Game Verification with Concurrency, Equilibria and Time
nodes.cite: M. Kwiatkowska, G. Norman, D. Parker, G. Santos, 2020. Proc. CAV 2020, LNCS 12225, pp. 475-487, Springer. DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-53291-8_25.
nodes.note: Extends the PRISM framework to turn-based and concurrent stochastic multi-player games with equilibria and time, enabling verification and strategy synthesis for adversarial or competitive protocol settings (security, energy). Game-theoretic companion to PRISM.

nodes.title: The Modest Toolset: An Integrated Environment for Quantitative Modelling and Verification
nodes.cite: A. Hartmanns, H. Hermanns, 2014. Proc. TACAS 2014, LNCS 8413, pp. 593-598, Springer. DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-54862-8_51.
nodes.note: An integrated, JANI-based environment for quantitative modelling and verification across probabilistic, real-time and hybrid automata, bundling the mcsta (exact) and modes (statistical) engines. A distinct ecosystem alongside PRISM/Storm, interoperable via the JANI exchange format.

nodes.title: Uppaal SMC Tutorial (statistical model checking of stochastic timed automata)
nodes.cite: A. David, K. G. Larsen, A. Legay, M. Mikucionis, D. B. Poulsen, 2015. Int. J. Software Tools for Technology Transfer (STTT) 17(4), pp. 397-415. DOI 10.1007/s10009-014-0361-y.
nodes.note: The statistical model checking engine of UPPAAL for networks of priced/stochastic timed automata, estimating performance and probabilistic properties by simulation where exact model checking is undecidable; directly relevant to performance evaluation of timed network protocols. Extends UPPAAL and applies the SMC method surveyed by Legay et al.

nodes.title: A SimEvents Model for the Analysis of Scheduling and Memory Access Delays in Multicores
